275:**Attended sessions dispatch lane-sensitive legs as headless `kimi -p` processes.** The
276-AgentSwarm/agent-calls shapes above are the UNATTENDED in-session path -- lanes bind there
277-only because `kimiGoalInvocation` (go.md step 6) already set the env pair for the whole run
278-loop. An ATTENDED/interactive session (a human driving this skill in the TUI) has no such
279-bind, and the TUI ignores `model_preference` entirely, so an in-session `Agent` call there
280-can never engage a lane. Lane-sensitive legs in an attended session therefore dispatch via
281-`kimiProcessDispatch({ brief, agentFile, cwd, lane })` (`src/kimi-dispatch.js`) -- one
282-headless `kimi -p` process per leg, spawned straight from the descriptor's `{ argv, env,
283-cwd, lane }`: `argv` is `["-p", brief, "--agent-file", <absolute agent file>,
284-"--output-format", "stream-json", "-m", KIMI_LANES[lane]]`, and `env` is the shared
285-`kimiLaneEnv()` OVERRIDE pair, carried for the v2 engine flag `--agent-file` needs (its
286-`KIMI_SECONDARY_MODEL` half also binds lanes for any subagents the leg itself spawns) --
287-merge it over the ambient process env at spawn (`{ ...process.env, ...d.env }`), never
288-pass it as the whole env (a wholesale replacement loses HOME/PATH and the child breaks). `-m` is ALWAYS
289-emitted, for the primary lane too: `model_preference` binds only a process's SPAWNED
290-SUBAGENTS, never the `-p` process's own main agent, so the process's model comes ONLY from
291-`-m` and omitting it silently falls to config `default_model`. The leg's receipt is the
292-stream-json result on stdout plus the process exit code, with per-leg token accounting from
293-`readSessionUsage` (`src/kimi-receipts.js`) over the fresh session dir the process writes
294-(docs/research/kimi-code-cli.md sec 8). Reserve the attended session's native `Agent` tool

610	- **muster does not write the MODEL half of `config.toml`.** It is a shared, user-owned file, and the
611	  hook-bombardment diagnosis is the standing lesson on muster mutating shared harness config. The
612	  install *reports* the required delta (`modelPreference.requiredConfig`) and leaves the edit to the
613	  user. Declining it is safe: with no secondary model configured, every agent inherits the caller's
614	  model and the stamps are inert. The **preferred** route is the per-process env pair
615	  `KIMI_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_FLAG=1` + `KIMI_SECONDARY_MODEL=kimi-code/kimi-for-coding`, which binds
616	  the lanes for a muster-launched `kimi -p` while mutating nothing and leaving the user's
617	  interactive sessions untouched. (`KIMI_SECONDARY_EFFORT` sets the lane's effort.) The ONE
618	  exception to "no config writes" (since 2026-07-26): `muster install kimi` merges a
619	  marker-delimited `[[permission.rules]]` deny block (the action-class fence, §4.2) into
620	  `config.toml` — a pure add/remove of muster's own block, never an edit of the user's settings.
621	
622	The gate is not optional: `model_preference` "applies only to newly spawned subagents when the
623	secondary-model experiment is enabled", and **"The TUI currently ignores this field."** Lanes bind
624	under `kimi -p` / `kimi web`, never in the interactive TUI. An explicit `model: "primary"|"secondary"`
625	on the `Agent`/`AgentSwarm` *call* overrides the profile — so muster can also tier per dispatch, not
626	just per profile (it is "ignored when resuming"; resumed subagents keep their model).
627	
628	**IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-27 — the env bind is live, closing the omission §6 flags as "not neutral."**
629	Until now the stamped lanes were inert on a real run: nothing in the live path set the env pair, so
630	with a secondary model configured every agent — judgment included — would have ridden the cheap
631	lane. The bind is now wired end to end: `kimiLaneBinding()` / `kimiLaneEnv()` (`src/kimi.js`) derive
632	the pair from `KIMI_TIERS` → `KIMI_LANES` as the single source (the lane models are whatever the
633	opus/sonnet families resolve to, checked against `KIMI_LANES` so a hand edit that drifts the two
634	apart fails loud); `kimiGoalInvocation` (`src/kimi-dispatch.js`) sets it on every muster-launched
635	`kimi -p "/goal …"` run — the go.md step-6 run loop — so the 27 stamped lanes engage on a real run;
636	lane-sensitive dispatches carry the per-call `model` override (`kimiAgentCall` derives the lane from
637	the shared manifest, so a dispatch never contradicts the stamped file); and `muster doctor` reports
638	the active binding (`kimi-lane-binding`). A config-side bind was rejected on the evidence: the
639	experiment flag is process-env only (the config schema's `[providers.<name>].env{}` is provider
640	credentials, not a flag surface), so the only config route is the `default_model`/`[secondary_model]`
641	edit the design call above already declines — per-process is the complete bind that mutates nothing.
